Hello! I am Stefano Sacco a Mechanical Civil engineer from the “Universidad de Chile” and I am doing an M.Sc. of Materials Engineer with Ph.D. Patricio Mendez as my advisor. 
I have always been a really curious person who wants to learn more about the major quantity of things that I can. I love sports and outdoors gatherings; I see myself as a social and enthusiastic person who likes to travel and see the world. 
I lived in Madrid for 8 months in 2016 as an exchange student at the “Universidad Autónoma de Madrid” and that opportunity was so awesome that I wanted to live abroad again. In 2020 I got the opportunity to do and internship in the Canadian Centre for Welding and Joining (CCWJ) and it was also a very good experience. Nevertheless, that opportunity got interrupted because of the Covid pandemic. 
In 2021, I won a scholarship to go study at MIT in Boston, but the in-person classes were cancelled so I did it online. In that time, I learned about Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science. I was impressed about how versatile the algorithms are and how they can be applied to almost everything. Undoubtedly the future is a mix between algorithms and human reasoning.
After finishing my Mechanical Engineering degree and the Machine Learning course, I was offered to do a M.Sc. at the University of Alberta and here I am. The experience of being a master student in Canada has been awesome, the people who I work with are really good and I truly recommend everyone to experience the CCWJ vibe.

## Project

In 2021, I started a project with AltaSteel, a steelworks company. The Canadian Centre for Welding and Joining (CCWJ) and AltaSteel have been partnering since 2012 doing different projects regarding hydrogen, nitrogen and oxygen in steels. 

My project consists mostly in create a model to estimate the hydrogen concentration in the billets and rods.  To achieve so the first step was to get a deeper understanding of the steel manufacturing and afterwards, find the crucial steps regarding hydrogen diffusion. As the hydrogen diffusion is related to the temperature of the process, the thermal analysis of the steelmaking plays a main role in its diffusion.  When the thermal analysis is done, the next step is to create a diffusion model and finally, validate it with experimental data.
